lessons.title: Basic Types
lessons.content:
# Basic Types

TypeScript extends JavaScript by adding static types.

### Common Types
- `string`, `number`, `boolean`
- `any`: Opt-out of type checking (use sparingly).
- `unknown`: Safer alternative to `any`.
- `void`: Used for functions that return nothing.
- `never`: For values that never occur (e.g., functions that always throw).

```typescript
let isDone: boolean = false;
let lines: number = 42;
let name: string = "Anders";
```

Enums
lessons.content:
# Enums

Allow you to define a set of named constants.

### Numeric Enums
```typescript
enum Direction {
  Up = 1,
  Down,
  Left,
  Right,
}
```

### String Enums
```typescript
enum Response {
  No = "NO",
  Yes = "YES",
}
```
Enums are real objects at runtime, unless they are `const enums`.

Utility Types
lessons.content:
# Utility Types

TypeScript provides several utility types to facilitate common type transformations.

- `Partial<T>`: Makes all properties in T optional.
- `Required<T>`: Makes all properties in T required.
- `Readonly<T>`: Makes all properties in T readonly.
- `Pick<T, K>`: Constructs a type by picking a set of properties K from T.
- `Omit<T, K>`: Constructs a type by picking all properties from T and then removing K.
